senses.gloss:
चर् चर्, cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) चरति, -ते,
चचार, चेरे, चरिष्यति, -ते, अचारीत्, चरि-
तुम् (ep. चर्तुम्, Ved. चरध्यै, चरितवे, च-
रसे), to move one's self, go, walk, move, stir, drive
(in a carriage &c.), roam about, walk about, wander,
(in these senses applied to men, animals, water, ships,
stars, &c.); to graze; to spread, be diffused; to be
active; move or travel through, pervade, go along,
follow; to behave, conduct one's self; to live, be,
remain in any position, act; to be engaged in,
occupied with, busy one's self with (with inst., e. g.
यज्ञेन चरति, he is engaged in a sacrifice); to
undertake, set about, undergo, observe, practise, do
or act in general (e. g. व्रतानि चेरुः, they observed
vows; and in this sense applied rather vaguely to
express various ideas, e. g. विघ्नं चरति, he puts
a hindrance; भैक्षं चरति, he begs; विवादं
चरति, he is engaged in a lawsuit; मृगयां
चरति, he hunts; सम्बन्धांश् चरति, he enters
into connections; मार्गं चचार वाणैः, he
made a way with arrows); to continue performing
or being (with a part., e. g. अर्चन्तश् चेरुः, they
continued worshipping; स्वामिनम् अवज्ञाय चरेत्,
he may go on despising his master); to exercise the
body with penance, e. g. तपसा इन्द्रियाणि चरेत्,
he should exercise his organs with penance; (with or
without मिथुन) to perform the act of copula-
tion, to have sexual intercourse with, have to do
with; to make or render (with two acc., e. g. न-
रेन्द्रं सत्य-स्थं चराम, let us make the
king keep his word); to act as a spy; to consume,
eat (e. g. मांसं चरेत्, let him eat flesh): Caus.
चारयति, -यितुम्, to cause to move or walk about;
to pasture; to send, direct, turn, move; to cause to
pervade; to drive away; to cause to practise or per-
form; to cause to copulate; to obtain knowledge of,
acquaint one's self with (with acc.); to doubt [cf.
वि-चर्]: Desid. चिचरिषति, to wish to act or con-
duct one's self; to be willing to deal with, to have
intercourse with: Intens. चर्चरीति, चञ्चूर्यते,
चञ्चुरीति, चञ्चूर्ति, to move quickly or repeat-
edly, to walk about, pervade; to act wantonly or
coquettishly; [cf. Lat. curro, currus; properus (?):
Hib. cara, ‘a leg or haunch;’ carachadh, ‘moving;’
carachd, ‘motion:’ Gr. κύρω, κυρέω: Goth. fara:
Germ. fahren: Old Germ. hor-sc: Eng. horse: Lith.
kieláuju, kielias, kielione: Old Pers. cartanay.]

चर, अस्, ई, अम्, moving, walking, going; loco-
motive, any animal (so named as moving in contra-
distinction to plants); movable, trembling, shaking,
unsteady; (at the end of comp.) going, walking,
wandering, being, living [cf. अधश्-चर, अन्त-
चर, अप्-च्˚, उपरि-च्˚, एक-च्˚, &c.]; following;
performing, practising (e. g. व्रत-चर, practising
vows). Sometimes चर is placed at the end of a
word as an affix in the sense of ‘having been formerly,’
e. g. आढ्य-चर, one who has been rich formerly;
देवदत्त-चर, having been formerly possessed by
Devadatta; (अस्), m. a spy, a secret emissary or
agent; a wagtail; a kind of small shell, Cypræa
[]
Moneta [cf. कपर्द]; a game played with dice and
men similar to backgammon; the planet Mars; a
cowrie; the seventh Karaṇa in astrology; the Karaṇas
collectively; the difference of time between the rising
of a heavenly body at Laṅkā or Ceylon, over which
the first meridian passes, and that of its rising at any
particular place; a term for particular lunar mansions
and for a particular number of the signs of the zodiac.
—चर-गृह, अम्, n. a moving or varying sign of
the zodiac, i. e. the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth.
—चर-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—चर-द्रव्य,
आणि, n. pl. movables, goods and chattels.
—चर-
पुष्ट, अस्, m. a mediator (lit. ‘nourished by a
spy’).
—चर-भ, अम्, n. a moving or varying
sign of the zodiac, i. e. the first, fourth, seventh, and
tenth; [cf. चर-गृह.]
—चर-भवन, अम्, n.
a moving or varying sign of the zodiac; [cf. the
preceding.]
—चर-मूर्ति, इस्, f. an idol which is
carried about in procession.
—१. चराचर (˚र-अच्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, movable and immovable, locomotive and
stationary, moving and fixed (as animals and plants);
(अम्), n. the aggregate of all created things, whether
animate or inanimate; the world; sky, atmosphere;
heaven, paradise; (ई), f. a young woman.
चार, अस्, m. a spy &c. See s. v.

चार चार, अस्, m. (fr. rt. चर्), = चर, a
spy, scout, secret agent or emissary, messenger;
going, motion, progression, course; wandering about,
travelling; proceeding; performing, practising; bind-
ing, a bond, fetter; a prison, a house of confinement;
the tree Buchanania Latifolia, = पियाल; (अम्), n. a
factitious poison, (for वार); [cf. Lat. carcer.]
—चार-काण्ड, अम्, n. ascensional difference (in
astronomy).
—चार-चक्षुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, ‘spy-eyed,’
i. e. a king or minister who uses spies as his eyes,
one who employs spies or agents and sees through
their medium; (उस्), n. espionage.
—चार-चण,
अस्, आ, अम्, graceful in gait or motion.
—चार-चुञ्चु,
उस्, उस्, उ, graceful in walking, of graceful carriage.
—चार-ज्या, f. the sine of the ascensional difference.
—चार-पथ, अस्, m. a place where two roads
meet.
—चार-भट, अस्, m. a valorous warrior.
—चार-वायु, उस्, m. summer air, zephyr.
—चारान्-
तरित (˚र-अन्˚), अस्, m. a secret emissary or spy.
—चारेक्षण (˚र-ईक्˚), अस्, m. a statesman, a
minister or king (who employs spies).

चरक, अस्, m. a wanderer, a wandering religious
student; a spy or secret emissary; N. of a Muni and
physician, (a legend relates that the serpent-king
Śeṣa, who was himself the recipient of the Āyur-veda,
once visited the earth, and finding it full of sickness and
suffering became moved with pity, and determined
to devise a scheme for alleviating disease; hence he
became incarnate as the son of a Muni and was called
Caraka because he had visited the earth as a kind of spy
or चर; he then composed a new book on medicine,
based on older works of Agni-veśa and other pupils
of Ātreya, which book was called after him); a kind
of plant, cf. पर्पट; (अम्), n. the title of the
treatise on medicine written by Caraka; (आस्), m. pl.,
N. of a branch of the Black Yajur-veda, the practices
and rites enjoined by which are different in some
respects from those in the Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa; (ई),
f. a kind of poisonous fish; N. of an evil spirit.
—चरक-ग्रन्थ, अस्, m. Caraka's book.
—च-
रक-तन्त्र-व्याख्या, f. title of a commentary by
Haricandra.
—चरक-भाष्य, अम्, n. title of a
commentary by an author named Kṛṣṇa.

चारक, अस्, इका, अम्, acting, setting to work,
proceeding; composed by Caraka; (अस्), m. a spy,
a secret agent or emissary; a driver, a herdsman,
a leader; an associate, a companion; a groom, a
horseman, a cavalier; a wandering Brāhmanical stu-
dent; a fetter, a bond, a prison; the plant Bucha-
nania Latifolia (= चार); N. of a man; (इका), f. a
female attendant; a cock-roach.
—चारक-त्रिरात्र,
अस्, m., N. of a festival.

चरण, अस्, m. a foot soldier; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a
foot; a pillar, a support, a prop; the root of a tree;
a single line of a verse, the fourth part of a stanza;
(in prosody) a dactyl; a sect, a school, a branch of
the Vedas; a race, a family; (अम्), n. moving,
going round or about, wandering, roaming, grazing;
course; acting, dealing, managing, conduct, per-
formance; fixed or instituted observances for any
class, age, or condition (as priesthood, manhood,
&c.); behaving, conduct of life, good or moral
conduct; practising, accomplishing; consuming, eat-
ing; a particular high number; [cf. द्वि-चरण,
पुरश्-चरण, रथ-च्˚; cf. also Gr. and Lat.
πέρνα, perna; Goth. fairzna; Germ. Ferse;
Lith. kulnis; Hib. cairine; Lat. crus ?].
—चर-
ण-कमल or चरण-किशलय, अम्, n. a lotus-
foot (lit. foot-lotus), a beautiful foot, the foot of a lover,
of a deity, &c.
—चरण-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen
at one's feet, prostrate.
—चरण-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m.
the joint of the foot, the ancle.
—चरण-दास, अस्,
m., N. of the author of the Guruśiṣya-saṃvāda
and of the poems entitled Nāciketūpākhyāna.
—चरण-न्यास, अस्, m. the trace of a foot, foot-
step.
—चरण-प, अस्, m. a tree.
—चरण-पतन,
अम्, n. falling at the feet, prostration.
—चरण-
पतित, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen at the feet, prostrate.
—चरण-पद्म, अस् or अम्, m. n. a lotus (like)
foot, the foot of a deity or lover.
—चरण-पर्वन्,
अ, n. ‘foot-joint,’ the ancle.
—चरण-पात, अस्, m.
tread, trampling; foot-fall.
—चरण-युग, अम्, n.
both the feet; two lines of a stanza.
—चरण-
व्यूह, अस्, m. title of a treatise.
—चरण-शुश्रूषा,
f. prostration.
—चरण-सेवा, f. service, devotion.
—चरणानमित (˚ण-आन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, bent or
bowed under the feet, trodden down.
—चरणा-
[]
भरण (˚ण-आभ्˚), अम्, n. an ornament for the
feet.
—चरणामृत (˚ण-अम्˚), अम्, n. foot-nectar,’
the water in which the feet of a Brāhman or spiritual
guide have been washed.
—चरणायध (˚ण-आय्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, having the feet for weapons; (अस्), m. a
cock.
—चरणारविन्द (˚ण-अर्˚), अम्, n. the lotus
(like) foot (of a deity, lover, &c.).
—चरणार्ध
(˚ण-अर्˚), अम्, n. the half of the foot; half of the
fourth of a stanza.
—चरणास्कन्दन (˚ण-आस्˚),
अम्, n. trampling, treading down with the feet.
—च-
रणोदक (˚ण-उद्˚), अम्, n. water in which the
feet of a venerable Brāhman or spiritual teacher have
been washed.
—चरणोपग (˚ण-उप्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
in contact with the feet, at the feet.

चारण, अस्, m. a wanderer, a pilgrim; a wandering
actor or singer, an actor of note, a dancer, a mime,
a bard, a herald; a celestial singer, a panegyrist of
the gods; a reader of scripture; a spy; N. of a
place.
—चारण-त्व, अम्, n. dancing (the art).
—चारण-दारा, आस्, f. pl. female dancers, actresses,
&c.
—चारण-विद्य or चारण-वैद्य or चारणा-
विद्य, आस्, m. pl., N. of a branch of the Atharva-veda.

चरणीय, nom. A., Ved. चरणीयते, to follow,
perform, be engaged in, carry on; (Sāy.) to desire
to go.
1. चरण्य, nom. P. चरण्यति, to move.
2. चरण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, foot-like, like a foot.
चरण्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. moving, movable.

चरत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, going, moving, going on; pro-
ceeding, acting, practising.

चरथ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. moving, living; capable of
moving, movable; (अस्, अम्), m. n. going, moving, wan-
dering; movableness; liveliness, life; a going, a way.

चारथ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. going, wandering or
moving about, going in a carriage.

2. चराचर, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. चर् reduplicated; for
1. see P. 317, col. 3), moving locomotive, running;
trembling, shaking, unsteady; wished, desired; (अम्),
n., N. of a small shell; [cf. कपर्द.]
चरि, इस्, m. an animal in general.

चरित, अस्, आ, अम्, gone, gone to, attained, prac-
tised; (अम्), n. going, moving, course; acting, doing,
practice, behaviour, acts, deeds, practices, adventures,
‘res gestæ;’ story; nature; fixed institute, proper or
peculiar observance; [cf. उत्तर-राम-चरित, दुश्-
चरित, सच्-च्˚, सह-च्, सु-च्˚.]
—चरित-गुणत्व,
अम्, n. (?) accompaniment, assistance; meritorious
conduct.
—चरित-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, (at the end of
compounds) containing or relating deeds or adven-
tures, made up of deeds.
—चरित-व्रत, अस्, आ,
अम्, performing an act of devotion.
—चरितार्थ
(˚त-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, attaining one's object, success-
ful in an undertaking, satisfied, effected, successful.
—चरितार्थ-त्व, अम्, n. the attainment of an aim,
successfulness, success.
—चरितार्थय, nom. P. चरि-
तार्थयति, to cause a person to attain his aim.
—च-
रितार्थिन्, ई, इनी, इ, desirous of success.
चारित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to go; distilled, &c.
चरितिन्. Cf. दुश्-चरितिन्.

चरित्र, अम्, n. a foot, leg; going; acting, behaving,
behaviour, habit, practice, acts, deeds, proceedings,
exploits; instituted and peculiar observance or con-
duct; adventures, story, history or account of any
one's deeds or exploits; nature, disposition; (आ), f.
the tamarind tree; [cf. चारित्र.]
—चरित्र-बन्-
धक, अस्, m. a friendly pledge, one of unequal
value to the loan.
—चरित्र-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, expe-
rienced, familiar with customs.

चरीत्र, अम्, n. behaviour, conduct, practice; [cf.
चरित्र.]

चारित्र, अस्, m., N. of a Marut; (आ), f. the tama-
rind tree; (अम्), n. proceeding, manner of acting,
conduct; good conduct, behaviour; good name or
character, reputation; peculiar observance or practice,
peculiarity of customs or conditions; a ceremony.
—चारित्र-कवच, अस्, आ, अम्, cased in the armour
of chastity.
—चारित्र-वती, f., N. of a Samādhi.

चरिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, capable of moving, movable,
locomotive, active, unsteady, wandering about; (उस्),
m., N. of a son of Manu Sāvarṇa; also of a son of
Kīrttimat and Dhenukā.
—चरिष्णु-धूम, अस्, आ,
अम्, Ved. having moving smoke, whose smoke goes
everywhere.

चर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be practised &c.; [cf.
चरितव्य.]
चर्तव्य चर्तव्य. See col. 1.

चर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be gone; to be practised or
performed &c.; (आ), f. going about, wandering, walk-
ing about, driving or going in a carriage; pervading,
visiting; course; proceeding, behaviour; due and
regular observance of all rites or customs, following
the rules of studentship; practising religious austeri-
ties, wandering about as a mendicant; performing,
practising, engaging in, practice, conduct [cf. कु-
चर्या]; behaviour, deportment, usage; eating; (अम्),
n. going about, wandering, driving in a carriage &c.;
proceeding, behaviour, conduct; [cf. ब्रह्म-चर्य,
[]
भिक्षा-च्˚, भैक्ष्य-च्˚.]
—चर्यावतार (˚या-
अव्˚), अस्, m. title of a Buddhist work.
चर्य चर्य. See p. 318, col. 1.

चार्य चार्य, अस्, m., N. of a despised caste,
the son of an outcast Vaiśya; (perhaps for अचार्य.)

2. चार्य, अम्, n. (fr. चर or चार), spying out,
espionage, information brought by spies.

चरट चरट, अस्, m. a wagtail; (ई), f. =
चरण्टी, चिरिण्टी, चिरण्टी.

चरम चरम, अस्, आ, अम्, m. pl. चरमे or
चरमास्, (said to be fr. rt. चर्), last, hinder, ultimate,
final; outermost; western, west; lowest, least; imme-
diately following; (अस् or अम्), m. or n. (?), a particular
high number; (अम्), ind. at last, at the end; चरमा
क्रिया, the final ceremony, the funeral ceremony.
—चरम-काल, अस्, m. the last moments, the
hour of death.
—चरम-क्ष्माभृत्, त्, m. the
western mountain behind which the sun and moon
are supposed to set.
—चरम-वैयाकरण, अस्,
m. an ignorant grammarian.
—चरम-शैर्षिक,
अस्, ई, अम्, having the head towards the west.
—च-
रमाचल (˚म-अच्˚), अस्, m. or चरमाद्रि (˚म-
अद्˚), इस्, m. = चरम-क्ष्माभृत् above.
—चर-
माजा (˚म-अजा), f., Ved. the last or smallest she-goat.
—चरमावस्था (˚म-अव्˚), f. the last state.
चरम्य, nom. P. चरम्यति, to be the last.
चरव्य चरव्य. See below under चरु.
चरव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, destined for the Caru oblation.

चरु चरु, उस्, m. a kind of vessel in which a
particular oblation is prepared, a saucepan, pot, kettle;
a cloud; an oblation of rice, barley, and pulse, boiled
with butter and milk for presentation to the gods or
manes.
—चरु-चेलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having portions of
offerings on the clothes (?); an epithet of Śiva;
(perhaps a wrong form for चारुचेलिन्.)
—चरु-
व्रण, अस्, m. a kind of cake.
—चरु-श्रपण,
अम्, n. sprinkling an oblation of milk and ghee.
—चरु-स्थाली, f. the vessel in which an oblation is
prepared, made either of clay or of udumbara-wood.
—चरु-होम, अस्, m. an oblation of a meat-offering.

चारु चारु, उस्, वी, उ (said to be fr. rt. चर्,
perhaps connected with 2. चन्), agreeable, welcome,
approved, esteemed, beloved, dear (with dat. or loc. of
the person, e. g. वरुणाय or वरुणे चारुः, dear to
Varuṇa), pleasing, lovely, beautiful, pretty, elegant;
(उस्), m. an epithet of Bṛhaspati; N. of a son of
Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī; of a Cakra-vartin; (री), f. a
beautiful woman; splendor; moonlight; intelligence;
N. of the wife of Kuvera; (उ), n. a various reading
for वर, saffron; [cf. Eng. fair; Brit. kaer.]
—चारु-कर्ण, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, having beautiful
ears.
—चारु-केशरा, f. a kind of grass, Cyperus, =
नागर-मुस्ता; a kind of tree, = तरुणी.
—चारु-
गर्भ, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa and Ruk-
miṇī.
—चारु-गीति, इस्, f. a kind of metre, a sort of
Gīti, containing 29+32 syllabic instants.
—चारु-
गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī.
—चारु-घोण, अस्, आ, अम्, handsome-nosed.
—चारु-
चित्र, अस्, m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—चारु-
ता, f. or चारु-त्व, अम्, n. loveliness, beauty.
—चारु-
दत्त, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman.
—चारुदत्त-ना-
मन्, आ, m. named Cāru-datta.
—चारु-दन्त, अस्,
m. ‘having beautiful teeth,’ N. of a merchant's son.
